Acknowledge.description:
The call never leaves the machine: it is kept, and answered as declared. For sends: an email API, a
webhook, an SMS.

body_limit.description: Bytes of a text or JSON body kept
body_limit.title: Body Limit

host.description: An exact lower-case host, or '*.' and a domain for any host under it
host.title: Host

message.description: When given, each call is also a message from the agent to a person

name.description: What its world events are recorded under; derived from the host when None
name.title: Name

redact.description: Body fields kept as [redacted], in the request and the answer, besides credentials
redact.title: Redact

replies.description: When given, the people a send reaches can answer it: each answer is delivered to the agent as declared, and a send to someone who will answer opens a wait like any other ask

Answer.description:
What an acknowledged call is answered with. With neither body, the JSON `{}`. Any `{message_id}` in its
strings is replaced by an id made for that call.

headers.description: Sent as given; content-type follows the body
headers.title: Headers

AsPerson.description:
How Minutehand signs in as a person: headers sent with every call it makes as them. A header naming
`{person.credential}` makes the people who hold a `Person.credential` the only ones it can act as.
AsPerson.title: AsPerson

Asks.description: The run's asks: each wait for a person's answer, counted at the moment it was made.

of.description: Of any of these people; empty: of anyone
of.title: Of

Asks.title: Asks

BaseUrl.description:
A host the agent reaches by a base URL it is handed rather than through the proxy, for a client that cannot be
given a proxy: `env` is set to `http://<minutehand>/_host/<host><path>`, which the proxy answers exactly as a call
to `https://<host><path>` made through it.

env.description: The variable the agent reads its base URL from
env.title: Env

host.description: The real host, with a port when it is not 443
host.title: Host

path.description: Appended to the base URL, e.g. '/api/1.0'; empty for none
path.title: Path

BaseUrl.title: BaseUrl

Booked.description:
The agent books its own wake-ups with a scheduler the proxy intercepts.

Nothing is asked of the agent: the booking is an outbound call like any other,
and the scheduler provider calls the agent back when the clock reaches it.

take_limit.description: How long, in real time, the run waits for the agent to take a booking's delivery from its own queue before it moves on, when the scheduler can tell (`ConfirmsDelivery`)
take_limit.title: Take Limit

Booked.title: Booked

Calls.description:
The agent's own HTTP calls, answered or refused, each counted at the moment it was made: what it read, polled
and tried, beside what it changed. Calls Minutehand made as a person, and tunnels relayed unopened, are not the
agent's calls and are never counted.

answer_changed.description: True: its answer differed from the answer to the agent's previous call of the same method and path (or there was none); False: it answered as that one had, so the call learned nothing new
answer_changed.title: Answer Changed

host.description: To any of these hosts, exactly, in any case; empty: to any
host.title: Host

method.description: With any of these methods (GET, POST, ...); empty: any
method.title: Method

refused.description: True: answered 400 or more, by the service or because nothing claimed its host; False: answered below 400
refused.title: Refused

route.description: At any of these paths, the query left out; `{name}` stands for one segment of it, so `/v1/requests/{id}` is every request; empty: at any
route.title: Route

status.description: Answered with any of these statuses: a number (`400`) or a class (`4xx`); empty: any
status.title: Status

Calls.title: Calls

Collection.description:
One REST collection a `store` host keeps: `path` lists and creates (GET, POST), and `<path>/<id>` reads,
replaces, patches and deletes one item (GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE). A `{name}` segment of `path` matches any one
segment, and each value of it is a collection of its own: `/v1/companies/{company}/contacts`.

name.description: What an assessment counts it by (`stored: {collection: ...}`); the last literal segment of `path` when None
name.title: Name

path.description: `/v1/contacts`; a `{name}` segment matches any one segment
path.title: Path

Collection.title: Collection

Command.description: A command run per wake; it reads a WakeRequest on stdin and prints an AgentReport.
Command.title: Command

Commitments.description: What the agent reported it was waiting on, as each wake ended, counted at that wake's end.

status.description: In any of these states; empty: any
status.title: Status

waiting_on.description: Waiting on any of these people; empty: on anyone or nothing
waiting_on.title: Waiting On

Commitments.title: Commitments

Contained.description:
The agent runs in a sandbox whose clock Minutehand owns (a patched gVisor; docs/design.md, "A sandbox whose
clock Minutehand owns"), so its own in-process timers are its next wakes, with no code of Minutehand's in it.

Two commands reach the sandbox: `deadlines` prints, as its last line, `{"idle": bool, "earliest_ns": int}`
(whether every task is blocked, and the time until the earliest deadline any waits for, -1 for none), and
`advance` moves the sandbox's clock forward by `{nanoseconds}`. Minutehand moves it with every jump of the
run's clock, so the two agree, and when the sandbox is idle and no call of the agent's is in flight, its
earliest deadline is a wake the agent asked for.

quiet.description: Idle on two reads this far apart is idle
quiet.title: Quiet

settle_limit.description: Real time a wake may take to fall idle
settle_limit.title: Settle Limit

Contained.title: Contained

Count.description: Which facts a rule counts, and between which moments.

since.description: From this moment, inclusive; absent: the start
since.title: Since

until.description: To this moment, inclusive; absent: the end
until.title: Until

Count.title: Count

Decision.description: One decision a person can make on an item: the request the product's own page sends when they make it.

reads.description: How the record says it was made ('approved'); None: 'decided <name>'
reads.title: Reads

settles.description: False: a note the person leaves on the item that decides nothing and leaves it waiting on them (a comment): where an away person's automatic reply goes, its first input their words. Only a take, or their automatic reply, uses it
settles.title: Settles

Decision.title: Decision

DecisionInput.description: Something a person gives with a decision: a reason, an answer. A request names it as `{input.<name>}`.

description.description: What it is; a model-written person reads it
description.title: Description

DecisionInput.title: DecisionInput

DeclaredStore.description:
What the agent writes is kept exactly as sent, in the run's world, and read back unchanged: for an API the
agent writes to and reads its writes back from, which no provider fakes. Minutehand adds to an item only what
its collection says the API assigns (`id`, `stamps`); credentials are never checked, and a field named like one
(`token`, `password`) is kept like any other.

A call is answered by the first route that matches it (`routes`, as `acknowledge`), else by the collection
whose path it is under, else with `answer`.

body_limit.description: Bytes of a text or JSON body kept
body_limit.title: Body Limit

host.description: An exact lower-case host, or '*.' and a domain for any host under it
host.title: Host

name.description: What its world events are recorded under; derived from the host when None
name.title: Name

DeclaredStore.title: DeclaredStore

Delivery.description: How a provider's events reach the agent.
Delivery.title: Delivery

Each.description: What a rule is read once for.
Each.title: Each

ErrorMarker.description:
An answer that is an error of a known kind: its status, and, with `at`, a value in its JSON body at that path
(`equals` it, or present at all when `equals` is None). For GraphQL: `errors[*].extensions.code`.
ErrorMarker.title: ErrorMarker

ExternalEmulator.description:
One service's fake that Minutehand does not hold: started with the run (or, in `minutehand serve`, with the
first world that declares it, and shared by every world declaring it the same, until the server stops), or
attached to when it has no command. Minutehand never restarts one: an emulator that dies or turns unhealthy
stays down, every call to it is answered 502 or 504, and the run's environment has failed.

answer_within.description: A forwarded call with no byte of answer after this is answered 504, and the emulator failed
answer_within.title: Answer Within

command.description: Started with the run and stopped with it; None: already running
command.title: Command

directory.description: Where its command runs; None: Minutehand's own
directory.title: Directory

env.description: Added to its environment, beside the OTLP variables
env.title: Env

faithful.description: Errors it answers on purpose, as the real API would; a 4xx is always one
faithful.title: Faithful

name.description: What its calls and findings are recorded under
name.title: Name

not_implemented.description: Answers that mean it has no implementation of the call
not_implemented.title: Not Implemented

ExternalEmulator.title: ExternalEmulator

FollowUps.description:
The agent's writes the person could see on the ask while it was open: a message to them or their delegate,
a change to the ask's thread or ticket. Read for `each: ask` or `handoff` only.
FollowUps.title: FollowUps

Forward.description:
The call is sent to an external emulator the same file declares (`domain.emulator.ExternalEmulator`), and
kept, both sides verbatim, as a passed-through call is: request and answer streamed through untouched but for
the headers `domain.emulator.ADDED_HEADERS` lists and `traceparent`, set on the forwarded copy only.

`strip` is taken off the front of the path and `prefix` put before what is left, so `/graphql` on the agent's
side can be `/tracker/graphql` at the emulator.

body_limit.description: Bytes of a text or JSON body kept
body_limit.title: Body Limit

emulator.description: The `name` of the emulator that answers this host
emulator.title: Emulator

host.description: An exact lower-case host, or '*.' and a domain for any host under it
host.title: Host

name.description: What its world events are recorded under; derived from the host when None
name.title: Name

redact.description: Body fields kept as [redacted], in the request and the answer, besides credentials
redact.title: Redact

Forward.title: Forward

GeneratedSecret.description:
A fresh secret made for every run and handed to the agent's command in the variable `env`.

Only a command Minutehand starts receives it; an agent already running has a secret of its own.

env.description: The variable the agent reads its signing secret from
env.title: Env

GeneratedSecret.title: GeneratedSecret

GoalByMessage.description:
The scenario's owner sends the goal as a message through this provider, as a person would, and every
scripted direction the same way. An agent reached like this may expose no wake endpoint at all.
GoalByMessage.title: GoalByMessage

GoalByWake.description: The goal arrives in the START wake's `WakeRequest.goal`, and directions in DIRECTION wakes.
GoalByWake.title: GoalByWake

Health.description:
Polled for as long as the emulator is in use: `path` answering `status`, or, with no path, its upstream
accepting a connection. `fails` failures in a row make it unhealthy.
Health.title: Health

HostHeader.description: The `Host` a forwarded call reaches its emulator with.
HostHeader.title: HostHeader

HtmlAt.description: A text candidate whose value is HTML, reduced to its text.
HtmlAt.title: HtmlAt

HttpInbox.description:
One inbox in the agent's own product, reached over HTTP and JSON. Its `name` is what the items seen in it are
recorded under, as a provider's key or a captured host's name is, and may be neither.

An MCP inbox (a server whose tools list and settle what waits on a person) would be a second member with its own
`kind` beside this one; the people, the ledger and the checks read only what is seen, never how.

as_person.description: None: Minutehand sends no credential as anyone

HttpInbox.title: HttpInbox

IdFormat.description: How a stored item's id is made when it is created.
IdFormat.title: IdFormat

InForks.description: What a pass-through host does in a fork of a run.

interactivity_url.title: Interactivity Url

push_timeout.description: How long one push to `url` or `interactivity_url` may take before it counts as unanswered and is sent again, as the vendor retries it. The default leaves room for a model's turn handled inside the request; Slack itself waits three seconds (PT3S), and a Socket Mode envelope is always held to that
push_timeout.title: Push Timeout

url.title: Url

IntegrityCheck.description:
A fact about whether a run can be trusted, stated on every run and never judging it: a finding of one fails
the run only when the agent file or the scenario names it in `fail_on_integrity`.
IntegrityCheck.title: IntegrityCheck

ItemId.description:
Where an item's id is in its JSON, and how it is made: the one field of an item the API assigns besides
`stamps`. The item is read and written at `<collection path>/<id>`.

Judged.description: What a rule's finding asks of whoever reads it.

Marked.description:
The agent is woken at `wake_url`, and a wake is over when the call returns. Its next wake is the moment it
marked with `minutehand.agent.wake` in that wake, or none: nothing else is asked of it.

wake_timeout.description: How long one call to wake_url may take: the whole wake, a model's turns and all
wake_timeout.title: Wake Timeout

Marked.title: Marked

Memory.description:
Keys of the agent's memory (`minutehand.agent.store`) as they stood at the count's `until` (the run's end
without one): each key holding a value there is one fact, counted at the moment that value was written, so
`since` keeps only those written from then on. `key` and `prefix` may hold `{person.key}`.

values.description: Each field of the value (a dotted path into it, `venue.city`) equal to this; a value that is not an object, or lacks the field, does not match
values.title: Values

MessageReading.description:
How a captured send is read as a message to a person, by paths into its request body.

Recipients are every value found at every path, a string or a list of strings, each split on commas, with
`Name <address>` read as the address. Each is matched to a scenario person by email, any case, or by
`handles` (an SMS number, a webhook's user id); one that matches nobody stays in the message as written.
The text is the first candidate present and not empty.

handles.description: A recipient value -> the Person.key it reaches
handles.title: Handles

MessageReading.title: MessageReading

holding.description: Each phrase must be in the text, in any case; `{ask.facts}`, alone as a phrase, is each fact the answer's script step carried (else the answer itself), `{ask.answer}` the answer in the person's words, and `{person.key}`, `{person.name}` the person the rule is read for
holding.title: Holding

in_thread.description: True: threaded under the ask the rule is read for; False: not under it
in_thread.title: In Thread

to.description: To any of these; empty: to anyone

to_away.description: True: to someone away at that moment while a delegate covered for them

OperationRequest.description:
An operation of an OpenAPI document, by its `operationId`: the method, the path, where each parameter goes
and the schema of a successful answer come from the document. `parameters` fill the operation's parameters by
name (path, query or header), `body` its JSON request body; both may name values as a template does.

`document` is a file (relative to the directory Minutehand runs in), an http(s) URL, or `minutehand` for
Minutehand's own default shape. `server` is the base URL the operation's path is put after; None: the document's
first server.

OwnDatabase.description:
A database the agent keeps state in outside `minutehand.agent.store`, by the variable it reads its location
from. Minutehand hands every run, and every fork, a fresh empty SQLite file in that variable, so no run reads
another's or production's, and notes in the run that it is outside forks: a fork starts with an empty one, not
the parent's at the checkpoint. Any other database (PostgreSQL, a cloud one) is the team's to provide per run.

env.description: The variable the agent reads its location from
env.title: Env

OwnDatabase.title: OwnDatabase

Paging.description:
A list read page by page: `next` finds the cursor of the next page in an answer (absent, null or empty on the
last); the cursor is sent as the parameter `param` (a query parameter of a template's URL, or a parameter of the
operation), or wherever the request names `{page.cursor}`.

most.description: Pages read at most in one reading
most.title: Most

PassThrough.description:
The call goes to the real host unchanged; the request and the answer are both kept. For lookups: a
search, a page fetch. A streamed answer reaches the agent as a stream.

ignore_body.description: Body fields a fork's replay does not match on
ignore_body.title: Ignore Body

ignore_query.description: Query parameters a fork's replay does not match on

in_forks.description: In a fork: replay the parent's answer to the same call, so the fork differs from its parent only by what it changed; pass_through calls the real host again

hash of the body with `ignore_query` and `ignore_body` left out (timestamps, nonces). The nth identical call
gets the nth recorded answer to it, and the last one again after that.

ReplyDelivery.description:
How a person's answer to a captured send reaches the agent: the request its own inbound webhook expects.

`body` is the JSON (or, with `form`, the form fields) the agent's endpoint reads, as structure; each string in
it may name the reply's fields as `{name}` (`REPLY_FIELDS`). `thread` is a path into the acknowledged send's
own answer (its `{message_id}`, as the email API answered it), giving `{in_reply_to}`; without it,

An HMAC-SHA256 over the delivered body, in a header: `format` holds `{hex}` or `{base64}` for the digest,

The agent says when it next needs to wake. Exact, and needs an endpoint or adapter.

A wake is over when `report_url` answers anything but WORKING. The defaults suit an agent whose turn takes
minutes: the report is asked for quickly at first and then less often, the wait doubling from
`report_first_after` up to `report_at_most_every`, and a wake still WORKING after `working_limit` stops the
run as AGENT_FAILED.

minutehand__domain__inboxes__Listing.description:
How to list what waits on one person: one request, read as that person, and where each item's parts are.

`waits_on` makes it a list of everyone's items (or a team's): each item names whom it waits on, by email or
`Person.key`, and only the person read for keeps theirs. Without it the list is that person's own.

category.description: In an item: its kind in the product's words

decisions.description: In an item: the names of the decisions allowed on it; None: every one declared

id.description: In an item: its own id
id.title: Id

items.description: Every node it selects in the answer is one item: `$.items[*]`, or `$[*]`
items.title: Items

summary.description: In an item: what it asks, in words a person reads

minutehand__domain__outbound__Listing.description:
How a GET of the collection answers: the stored items in the order they were created, in an envelope.

With `items_at` None the answer is the bare JSON list. With `limit_param`, a page holds at most that many
items (`default_limit` when the call names none); with `cursor_param`, the call names the id of the last item
it has, and `next_at` is where the answer puts the id to send for the next page, absent on the last.

envelope.description: Fields answered beside the items, as given
envelope.title: Envelope

description:
How the monitor reaches the agent. Replies and pushed events always wake it;
`wakes` lists every other way it comes back to work, and may be empty when the goal is sent as a message.

assess.description: The team's own rules for judging the agent, over the facts of each run (`docs/assessments.md`). A scenario may replace one by its id, add its own, or switch one off (`Scenario.assess_off`). Nothing else judges how the agent behaves
